runs.content: Thermo Fisher Scientific picked up at today's close ($603.18) — a life-sciences/diagnostics leader up 33.4% over 3 months with a fresh CLSA Outperform initiation ($748 PT, ~24% upside), chosen as a defensive Burry-aligned name with zero AI-capex/semiconductor exposure. RELX was exited discretionarily (−7.72%, −$77) to keep the book at 35 open positions after TMO's entry — no mechanical stop-losses or signal exits on the other 33 continuing positions amid a fourth consecutive oil/yield-driven risk-off session (Dow −0.6%, S&P −0.58%, Nasdaq −0.65%). DHI is now the weakest continuing position at −7.15%, no Burry conflict. Portfolio net P&L: +$1,692 (+2.87% on $59,000).

SAP SE picked up at the previous close ($209.14) — a ~31% discount to Morningstar's $302 wide-moat fair value, with cloud backlog +27% YoY and full-year cloud guidance reaffirmed despite a trimmed operating-profit guide and a Buy→Neutral downgrade (PT raised to €201). BR was exited discretionarily (−8.18%, −$82) to keep the book at 35 open positions after SAP's entry — no mechanical stop-losses or signal exits on the other 33 continuing positions amid a second consecutive oil-driven risk-off session (Brent >$100/bbl on Iran-conflict escalation). RELX is now the weakest continuing position at −6.55%, no Burry conflict. Portfolio net P&L: +$1,835 (+3.16% on $58,000).
